newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Trussardi plans New York listing -magazine.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Trussardi plans New York listing -magazine.

text.p: Italian stylist Nicola Trussardi is reorganising his fashion group ahead of a planned Wall Street listing by next year, weekly financial magazine Il Mondo reported.

After the reorganisation, involving Milan-listed real estate company Rotondi of which Trussardi is chairman, one holding company, Finos, will control both the Trussardi group and Rotondi, Il Mondo said.

"The 23 percent of Rotondi currently in Finos's portfolio could be placed on the market or sold to other shareholders, industrial firms or ones in the distribution sector," Trussardi was quoted as telling Il Mondo. Trussardi SpA would end up by controlling brand management and distribution.

Il Mondo said that either Trussardi SpA or Finos could be quoted on Wall Street. The Trussardi group is expected to post 1997 global turnover of 800 billion lire ($439 million) against 700 billion lire in 1996. No-one was available for comment at Trussardi.

Meanwhile, Milan daily Corriere della Sera said in an unsourced report on Friday that advisors to the fashion house of Gianni Versace who was murdered last month were working on a planned Milan bourse listing next spring.
There was no available comment from the fashion house.
Versace, who was shot to death outside his Miami mansion, was believed to be planning, with his brother Santo and sister Donatella, a stock listing in Milan by June 1998.

Corriere said investment bank Morgan Stanley, for a long time an official Versace consultant, was working on the financial aspects of a listing while the Nicholson "head-hunter" firm had been mandated to reinforce Versace top management.
The Versace group posted 1996 net profit of 67 billion lire on turnover of around 850 billion lire.
